brief.offer: Expense policy templates for mid-size finance teams

facts.claim: Ramp offers an all-in-one financial operations platform covering cards, expenses, bill payments, procurement, vendor management, travel, banking, and accounting automation.
facts.excerpt: More than 70,000 businesses use Ramp to manage corporate cards, expenses, bill payments, procurement, vendor management, travel, banking, and accounting automation in one system.

facts.claim: Ramp says customers have saved more than $12 billion and 27.5 million hours using its platform.
facts.excerpt: Ramp customers have saved more than $12 billion and 27.5 million hours by using Ramp's controls, automation, and savings insights.

facts.claim: Ramp reports supporting more than $100 billion in annualized card and AP payment volume, with customers saving 5% or more on average.
facts.excerpt: Ramp supports more than $100 billion in annualized card and AP payment volume, and customers save 5% or more on average with Ramp.

facts.claim: Ramp’s customer stories include Eventbrite, whose CEO Julia Hartz praised the value Ramp brought to its finance team and global employee base.
facts.excerpt: Ramp has brought tangible value to our finance team, our global employee base, and to me personally. I am obsessed with Ramp.
facts.source_title: Ramp Customers are Happy Customers - Case Studies | Ramp

facts.claim: In June 2026, Ramp announced a $750 million financing round at a $44 billion valuation.
facts.excerpt: Today, Ramp announced a $750 million primary financing round led by ICONIQ, GIC, and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, valuing the company at $44 billion.
facts.source_title: Ramp Raises Series F at $44 Billion Valuation

facts.claim: Ramp said it had released more than 70 products and major features in the preceding few months and planned to begin serving companies headquartered in the UK and Europe that summer.
facts.excerpt: In the past few months, Ramp released 70+ products and major features, closed two acquisitions — Billhop (UK/EU payments) and Juno (guest travel) — and announced it would start serving companies headquartered in the UK and Europe this summer.
facts.source_title: Ramp Raises Series F at $44 Billion Valuation

facts.claim: Ramp announced a multi-year partnership making it the official expense management partner of Stanford Athletics.
facts.excerpt: Stanford Athletics and Ramp today announced a multi-year partnership naming Ramp the official expense management partner of Stanford Athletics.
facts.source_title: Stanford Athletics Selects Ramp to Modernize Financial Operations in Multi-Year Partnership - Stanford Cardinal - Official Athletics Website

research.website_note: Ramp’s website identifies Ramp Business Corporation and presents Ramp’s financial products and services.
research.gaps: No further detail on the intended recipient, specific outreach angle, or which product area is most relevant.

strategy.observation: In June 2026, Ramp announced plans to begin serving companies headquartered in the UK and Europe that summer.
strategy.offer_link: Expense policy templates could give Ramp’s Head of Content a practical resource for mid-size finance teams evaluating expense management as Ramp enters these markets. The templates could serve as a starting point for downloadable content, subject to review for local requirements.
hypotheses: Ramp’s content team may be developing educational resources to support the planned UK and European expansion.
Mid-size finance teams in those markets may find editable expense policies useful when evaluating expense management software.
The offered templates may add value beyond Ramp’s existing content, but that would need to be checked.
strategy.angle: With Ramp’s announced UK and European expansion, would expense policy templates be useful for content aimed at mid-size finance teams in those markets?
strategy.fit_reason: The offer is directly relevant to expense management and could be packaged as a practical content asset by this recipient. Its incremental value depends on Ramp’s existing template library and whether the templates suit the new markets.

draft.subject: Expense templates for Europe
draft.body:
Ramp’s plan to start serving UK- and Europe-based companies looks like a good moment for practical content.

I put together expense policy templates for mid-size finance teams. They’re meant as a starting point for downloadable content that a finance team can adapt before roll-out.

I help create these kinds of resources because they give buyers something concrete to use while they’re evaluating tools.

If you’re building content for those markets, should I send a sample template set for review?
